eilen.et: From Middle High German īlen, from Old High German īlen, from Proto-West Germanic *īlijan (“to make haste, hasten”).

s: an island, usually a small and/or isolated one

Eiland.et: From Middle High German eilant, einlant, from Middle Low German eilant (by which it was reinforced again during the 16th c.), from Old Frisian eiland, from Proto-West Germanic *auwjuland, from Proto-Germanic *awjōlandą. Cognate with Dutch eiland, English islan…

Eileiter.et: From Ei (“egg”) + Leiter (“ladder/conductor”), from leiten (“to lead”).

eilig.et: From Middle High German īlig, from Old High German īlīg, from Proto-West Germanic *īlīg. Equivalent to Eile + -ig.
